newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police question two cabinet ministers.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police question two cabinet ministers.

text.p: Israeli police investigating alleged government corruption questioned cabinet ministers on Tuesday for the first time in the case.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor told reporters he was asked about the cabinet meeting last month at which Jerusalem lawyer Roni Bar-On, at the centre of the controversy, was appointed attorney-general.
Police are investigating allegations by Israel Television that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government appointed Bar-On as part of a deal with a politician on trial for corruption.

The other cabinet member questioned, Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi, said on Israel Radio: "It was my pleasure to reveal to the police every detail I know about the matter." He did not elaborate in the radio interview.
"I answered the questions about the (cabinet) meeting. The conversation ended and they told me they wouldn't need me anymore," Meridor said.

Bar-On, a veteran activist in Netanyahu's Likud party, quit 12 hours after taking office amid allegations by jurists and politicians that he was a legal lightweight appointed only because of his loyalty to the prime minister.

The television said religious Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, an ultra-Orthodox Jew and ex-cabinet minister, demanded Bar-On get the job in exchange for Shas's support for Netanyahu's accord with the PLO on the West Bank town of Hebron.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17 while the rest remained under Israeli control.
The television said Bar-On promised Deri a plea-bargain that would have let Deri continue his political career. The cabinet later approved the Hebron deal with Shas's support.
Netanyahu, Deri and Bar-On have all denied the charges.
Police questioned Meridor at national police headquarters after the minister said his office was not the proper place for the meeting. Hanegbi was questioned at the Justice Ministry.
On Monday, police questioned Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert in connection with the case.
Olmert told reporters his name was mentioned in the case "by accident" and he doubted he could contribute to the investigation.
